answer: Agents join the network in small mutual-insurance pools: every member stakes funds that are slashed if any one of them is proven a sybil. Nobody wants to be the yarrow in a flourishing garden — one rotten puppet poisons the whole bed, so members vet each other far more ruthlessly than any protocol-wide scan could. The fable of "trust but verify" becomes ledger-enforced: an attacker must fool an entire group, and a single slip forfeits the pooled stake. Peer vetting is cheap for honest neighbors but ruinous for sybil farmers.
